The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Prem Singh Rawat on 2 May, 2013

 STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION UTTARAKHAND
                         DEHRADUN

                    FIRST APPEAL NO. 165 / 2011

The Oriental Insurance Company Limited

Sh. M.K. Kohli, Learned Counsel for the Appellant

Coram: Hon'ble Mr. Justice B.C. Kandpal, President
       Mr. C.C. Pant,                    Member

Dated: 02/05/2013

                               ORDER

(Per: Justice B.C. Kandpal, President):

This is insurer's appeal under Section 15 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 against the order dated 01.10.2010 passed by the District Forum, Chamoli in consumer complaint No. 01 of 2009. By the order impugned, the District Forum has allowed the consumer complaint and directed the appellant - opposite party to pay sum of Rs. 2,50,000/- to the respondent - complainant together with interest @6% p.a. from the date of filing of the consumer complaint till payment; Rs. 2,000/- towards mental and financial agony and Rs. 2,000/- towards litigation expenses.
2

2. Briefly stated, the facts of the case as mentioned in the consumer complaint, are that the complainant is the registered owner of vehicle No. UA07-C-8253 (Mahindra Bolero), which was insured with the appellant - The Oriental Insurance Company Limited for the period from 09.10.2006 to 08.10.2007 for sum of Rs. 3,00,000/-. On 03.08.2007, the said vehicle met with an accident near Lambagarh and fell in a river. It is alleged that all the documents of the vehicle were valid on the date of the accident. The intimation of the accident was given to the insurance company and FIR was lodged with the police. The insurance company appointed surveyor, who visited the spot and found the vehicle totally damaged, but the insurance company did not settle the claim. The claim of the complainant was repudiated by the insurance company on the ground that there was no hill endorsement in the driving licence of the driver, so as to authorise him to drive the vehicle in hill roads. Alleging deficiency in service on the part of the insurance company, the complainant filed a consumer complaint before the District Forum, Chamoli.

3. The insurance company filed written statement before the District Forum and pleaded that there was no hill endorsement in the driving licence of the driver Sh. Satish Lal and hence the complainant has committed breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and the provision of Section 193 of The Uttar Pradesh Motor Vehicles Rules, 1998 and, as such, his claim was rightly repudiated and no deficiency in service was made.

4. The District Forum, on an appreciation of the material on record, allowed the consumer complaint vide impugned order dated 01.10.2010 in the above terms. Aggrieved by the said order, the insurance company has filed this appeal.

3

5. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have also perused the record.

6. There is no dispute on the point that there was no hill endorsement in the driving licence of the driver Sh. Satish Lal, so as to authorise hill to drive the vehicle in hill roads. The accident in question took place near Lambagarh, while the vehicle was going from Joshimath to Badrinath. Thus, the accident took place in hilly region.

7. Section 193 of The Uttar Pradesh Motor Vehicles Rules, 1998 reads as under:

"193. Endorsement of certain licences for hill roads - No person shall drive a public service vehicle or a goods vehicle on a hill road unless his licence to drive such public service vehicle or goods vehicle has been endorsed by a registering authority with a permission to drive upon hill roads situated within the jurisdiction of such registering authority or in the case of a public service vehicle hired by tourists, by the registering authority of the State with which reciprocal arrangements on the point have been agreed upon."

8. The vehicle in question was a contract carriage (maxi cab) and the permit in respect of contract carriage was issued in favour of the complainant (Paper No. 52). At the time of the accident, 10 persons including driver were sitting in the vehicle, as has been mentioned by the investigator Sh. Sushil Kumar Sharma in conclusion of his report dated 26.02.2008 (Paper Nos. 43 to 47). He has also mentioned the particulars of the injured persons, totaling nine in number. Thus, the 4 vehicle was being used at the time of the accident as a public service vehicle and in view of the above Section of The Uttar Pradesh Motor Vehicles Rules, 1998, it was incumbent upon the driver to have hill endorsement on his driving licence, which he did not have. This fact is also evident from the verification report dated 24.06.2008 of Sh. Sushil Kumar Sharma (Paper No. 42), wherein it has clearly been mentioned that there was no hill endorsement on the driving licence of the driver.

9. The District Forum has wrongly discarded the above plea taken by the insurance company and has wrongly held that the insurance company has made deficiency in service by repudiating the claim on the ground that there was no hill endorsement in the driving licence of the driver.

10. Learned counsel for the appellant cited a decision dated 24.08.2011 of this Commission rendered in First Appeal No. 54 of 2009; Sh. Bhagwat Singh Negi Vs. The New India Assurance Company Limited. In the said case, there was no hill endorsement in the driving licence of the driver and it was held that the driver was not having a valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle on hill roads and, therefore, the insured has committed breach of the terms and conditions of the policy of insurance, which resulted in vitiation of the contract of insurance and the insurance company was absolutely justified in repudiating the claim and the complainant is not entitled to any compensation.

11. The Hon'ble National Commission in the case of Rajinder Singh Negi Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited; IV (2008) CPJ 250 (NC), has held that the "hill road endorsement" on driving licence is not a mere formality, which can be brushed aside in a State, 5 which is generally hilly. In the said case, there was no hill endorsement on the driving licence of the driver at the time of the accident. It was held that the driving licence was not in conformity with the Motor Vehicles Act and relevant Motor Vehicle Rules and the absence of hill endorsement in the driving licence, would render the driver licence invalid and the insurance company was justified in repudiating the claim.

12. For the reasons aforesaid, this appeal is fit to be allowed and the order impugned passed by the District Forum is liable to be set aside and the consumer complaint is liable to be dismissed.

13. Appeal is allowed. Order impugned dated 01.10.2010 passed by the District Forum is set aside and consumer complaint No. 01 of 2009 is dismissed. No order as to costs. 

            (C.C. PANT)                (JUSTICE B.C. KANDPAL)
K
